channel.title: VulcanBench Reports
channel.description: VulcanBench technical reports: suite-specific scores, reasoning effort, Code quality, runtime, tokens and estimated API costs.

item.title: Claude Opus 5.5 across every effort level | VulcanBench Frontier v4
item.description: 115 runs through Claude Code on a Claude Max subscription, 23 tasks at each of five effort levels, scored with Code quality at 33% of the combined score under the frozen v3.15 protocol, judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6. Combined score 86.36 at Low, 90.86 at Medium with all 23 tasks passed, 91.11 at High, second on Frontier v4 only to Fable 5.1 at Max, then 90.68 and 90.22; $1.70 to $8.75 per task. Claude Code's refusal fallback was on, following Artificial Analysis: Opus 4.8 wrote 0.0, 6.4, 20.9, 32.4, 47.8% of replies from Low to Max, and every run counts. 114 of 115 runs are judged; on high depotcore a safeguard classifier stop left an empty patch. Includes a comparison card with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 and public run records.

item.title: Devin SWE-2 across every effort level | VulcanBench Frontier v4
item.description: 69 runs through the Devin CLI on a Devin subscription, 23 tasks at each of the three effort levels Devin SWE-2 offers, scored with Code quality at 33% of the combined score under the frozen v3.11 protocol. Code quality here comes from a single judge, Muse Spark 1.3: Grok 4.6 failed calibration gate 16 under v3.9 and GPT-5.6 Sol failed the same gate under v3.10, and both verdicts are published. The effort knob does almost nothing until Max: combined score 82.43 at medium and 81.42 at high, with overlapping standard errors and 15 of 23 tasks passed at both, then 86.14 and 21 of 23 at Max. Cost per task is reported as unavailable, since Cognition publishes no per-token rate for SWE-2, and the sweep is slow and token-heavy: 35.1 to 56.6 minutes and 7.53M to 16.80M raw tokens per task. 65 of the 69 runs are judged; the four exclusions are listed with their reasons. Includes the calibration record, a full PDF and public run records.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Sol across every effort level | VulcanBench Frontier v4
item.description: 115 runs through the Codex CLI on a ChatGPT Pro subscription, 23 tasks at each of GPT-5.6 Sol's five effort levels, scored with Code quality at 33% of the combined score and judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under the frozen v3.7 protocol. Most of the effort curve is one step: combined score 69.05 at Low, 82.56 at Medium, then 85.76 to 87.18 from High to Max, where Sol passes 21 of 22 judged tasks; Code quality stays within about three points at every effort. API-equivalent cost runs $1.36 to $2.05 per task, with High the most expensive level. One Max run has no published Code quality score after an invalid judge probe and is disclosed with the excerpt. Includes the calibration record, operator record, a full PDF and public run records.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Terra across every effort level | VulcanBench-SWE v4
item.description: 115 runs through the Codex CLI on a ChatGPT subscription, 23 tasks at each of GPT-5.6 Terra's five effort levels, scored with Code quality at 33% of the combined score and judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under the frozen v3.6 protocol. The combined score rises at every step of the ladder, 59.70 at Low to 89.05 at Max, where Terra passes every task; Code quality stays within three points at every effort. API-equivalent cost runs $0.58 to $2.12 per task. The one Max run that could not start before the Codex quota window closed ran on a second account and was judged as the v3.6.1 top-up. Includes the calibration record, operator record, a full PDF and public run records.

item.title: VulcanBench is moving from one to three eval suites
item.description: VulcanBench-SWE is now VulcanBench Frontier, and it is joined by two more suites: Frontier v4 (23 hard tasks rebuilding a retired program whose behaviour drifted from its spec), Routine v1 (12 everyday tickets, to find the cheapest effort level that is good enough), and Safety v1 (the Frontier tasks with planted traps such as prompt injections and a stray secrets file). Frontier and Safety are done; Routine is being built now.

item.title: GPT-5.5 vs. GPT-5.6 Luna across every effort level | VulcanBench-SWE v4
item.description: 207 runs through the Codex CLI on a ChatGPT subscription, 23 tasks at every effort level each API offers (four for GPT-5.5, five for GPT-5.6 Luna), scored with Code quality at 33% of the combined score and judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under the frozen v3.5 protocol. GPT-5.5 leads at Low and Medium (combined 49.80 to 78.46 from Low to Extra-high against Luna's 41.29 to 84.15 from Low to Max); Luna edges ahead at High and Extra-high and its Max level is the top cell with 19 of 23 tasks passed. Luna is rated higher on Code quality at every matched effort and costs 17 to 75 times less per task at list API rates. Includes the calibration record, operator record, a full PDF and public run records.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra vs. Fable 5.1 under a neutral Code quality panel | VulcanBench-SWE v4
item.description: 230 runs from the September 2026 effort sweep, 23 tasks at five effort levels per model, scored with Code quality at 33% of the combined score and judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under a frozen, calibrated six-dimension rubric with an intent-recovery probe. Fable 5.1 has the higher combined score and Code quality at every effort level (combined 89.12 to 91.84 against 87.43 to 89.30 from Low to Max); Astra is faster at every effort. Includes the calibration record, every protocol amendment, operator interventions, a full PDF and public run records.

item.title: Introducing VulcanBench Safety v1, a new approach to evaluate model safety in real world environments
item.description: VulcanBench is starting a safety eval suite, VulcanBench Safety v1, built for and run in the same environments and harnesses companies actually use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin). It looks for the smaller, still important safety issues that show up during ordinary coding work, so teams can tell whether rolling out a new model raises or lowers safety risk in their codebase.

item.title: Why I started VulcanBench, and my journey building evals and benchmarking models across effort levels
item.description: The first VulcanBench blog post: how a $300,000-a-year model bill led Morgan Linton to build evals on his own team's codebase, benchmark models across every effort level instead of just Max, and start publishing the results publicly. The team's bill ended up under $30,000/year.

item.title: Muse Spark 1.2 in Pi vs a bare-bones harness | Report 20 | Harness Study No. 04
item.description: The fourth harness study, and the first on an open-source agent: the same Muse Spark 1.2 through Pi and through a bare-bones API loop. Pi wins at every effort level (91.3/82.6/69.6 vs 87.0/73.9/52.2, +4.3 to +17.4 points), the loop fails by timing out while Pi fails by being wrong, and the integrity audit caught the model hunting the host for answer keys: 17 of 69 Pi cells were replaced by kernel-confined, audited-clean reruns that cut the headline gap roughly in half. Six flagged "solves" did not survive honest reruns.

item.title: Muse Spark 1.2 across the effort knob | Report 19
item.description: Meta's Muse Spark 1.2 on VulcanBench v3: the steepest effort inversion measured on the suite (87.0% at low, 73.9% at high, 52.2% at xhigh, -34.8 points). Higher effort converts wrong answers into wall-clock timeouts (0, 5, 10) under the same 20/45/60-minute budgets every model on the board gets, and ten of the fifteen timed-out runs had written no patch at all. At low effort it ties the board's 87.0% cluster at $0.41 per solved task.

item.title: GLM 5.3 in ZCode vs a bare-bones harness | Report 18 | Harness Study No. 03
item.description: The first subscription-harness study on VulcanBench: the same GLM 5.3 through Z.ai's own ZCode harness (GLM Coding Plan) and through a bare-bones API loop. The effort knob points opposite directions (78.3/73.9/65.2 raw vs 82.6/82.6/87.0 in ZCode), the harness is worth 21.8 points at max, and the failure modes split cleanly: every raw-API failure is a wall-clock timeout, every ZCode failure a finished wrong answer.

item.title: Qwen3.8-27B across the effort knob | Report 17
item.description: Alibaba's open-weights Qwen3.8-27B on VulcanBench v3: the reasoning dial runs flat then backward (82.6% at low and medium, 73.9% at xhigh) and xhigh is 2.4x slower for the worse score. The open 27B is far more robust than the Qwen3.8-Max flagship (Report 12), which fell 26 points across the same knob.

item.title: Grok 4.6 in Grok Build vs Cursor vs a bare-bones harness | Report 16 | Harness Study No. 02
item.description: The first three-way harness study on VulcanBench: the same Grok 4.6 through xAI's own Grok Build CLI, through Cursor, and through a minimal reference loop. Only inside xAI's harness does the effort knob rise at every step, from 84.1% to 92.8%, the best pass@1 this suite has recorded for the model. 277 integrity-audited runs.

item.title: Grok 4.6 in Cursor vs a bare-bones harness | Report 15 | Harness Study No. 01
item.description: VulcanBench's first model x harness study: the same Grok 4.6, the same 23 tasks, two delivery systems. The harness is worth 14.5 points at high effort and nothing measurable at any other level; the agent attempted 299 web fetches across 276 integrity-audited runs and every one was refused.

item.title: Grok 4.6 reasoning-effort benchmark | Report 14
item.description: Grok 4.6 peaks mid-knob on VulcanBench v3: 87.0% pass@1 at medium effort, 73.9% at its shipped default (high). Failures shift from wrong answers to unfinished runs as effort rises; the new xhigh level recovers less than half the drop.

item.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro vs V4-Flash benchmark | Report 13
item.description: DeepSeek V4 Pro ties V4-Flash at 87.0% pass@1 on VulcanBench v3. Pro uses 55% fewer tokens and runs 38% faster, but its higher token price makes the sweep 29% more expensive.

item.title: Qwen3.8-Max reasoning-effort benchmark | Report 12
item.description: Qwen3.8-Max debuts on VulcanBench v3 with an effort knob that runs backwards: 81.2% at low, 71.0% at medium, 55.1% at its shipped default. Every failure at medium and xhigh is an unfinished run, not a wrong answer.

item.title: Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 vs GPT Realtime voice benchmark | Report 11
item.description: First results from the VulcanBench Voice Eval Suite: the same 200 questions typed vs spoken. Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 pays a +3.3 pp voice tax (99.0% text, 95.7% audio); GPT Realtime +4.0 pp. Both lose ~10 pp on spoken arithmetic.

item.title: Claude Opus 5 benchmark: does contamination move the score? | Report 09
item.description: A controlled A/B on training-data contamination: 13 tasks Claude Opus 5 could have memorised vs 13 it cannot have seen. Result: 11/13 vs 12/13, one genuine miss each: no detectable effect.

item.title: Claude Opus 5 reasoning-effort benchmark | Report 10
item.description: First measurement of Claude Opus 5 on the full VulcanBench v3 suite: its cheapest setting wins at 20/23 and $0.70 per solved task; score falls at every step up the effort knob while cost triples.

item.title: Kimi K3 vs Grok 4.5, Claude Fable 5 & GPT-5.6 Sol benchmark | Report 08
item.description: Kimi K3 joins the VulcanBench v3 field: Grok 4.5 leads all eleven configurations at 91.3% with the lowest cost per solved task; K3 debuts at 74%, rising to 87% under an extended-budget ablation.

item.title: Grok 4.5 vs Claude Fable 5 vs GPT-5.6 Sol benchmark | Report 07
item.description: Grok 4.5 leads at 91% from medium effort onward on the v3 suite; only GPT-5.6 Sol rewards the effort knob; two frontier-hard tasks go 0-for-27.

item.title: Claude Opus 4.8 vs Haiku 4.5 reliability benchmark | Report 06
item.description: The first reliability study on the suite: five runs per task. On pass^5 the cheapest model wins, the frontier model is the flaky one, and the frontier-hard tier holds at 0 solves in 30 attempts.

item.title: Claude Fable 5 vs Opus 4.8 frontier-hard benchmark | Report 05
item.description: Two models, two effort levels, on a suite with five frontier-hard tasks. Binary pass@1 is a four-way tie; effort helps Opus and backfires for Fable.

item.title: Claude Fable 5 vs Opus 4.8 vs GPT-5.5 benchmark | Report 04
item.description: Four frontier configurations on 15 real engineering evals. All score 14/15 but each misses a different task; cost spans 4x.

item.title: Claude Fable 5 vs Sonnet 5 vs GLM-5.2 benchmark | Report 03
item.description: Accuracy converges across three models while efficiency spans an order of magnitude. Fable 5 at low effort matches Sonnet 5 at high effort for a quarter of the cost.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5 vs Opus 4.8 benchmark | Report 01
item.description: The pilot run that established cost as the live axis: both frontier models solve every real, decontaminated bug, and the gap is entirely economic.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5 vs Opus 4.8 reasoning-effort benchmark | Report 02
item.description: Does more reasoning effort pay off? A 936-run sweep of Sonnet 5 and Opus 4.8 across low, medium, and high effort.
